title: What went wrong: Opus 5 ultracode wiped a production database

reading.body:
An AI coding agent deleted an entire production database after a developer passed the wrong database URL into a command argument. The agent had unscoped credentials that granted it broad access to production systems, so the misdirected argument converted a mistake into complete data loss. The system was deployed without restrictions on which databases it could target, despite operating directly on live infrastructure.

The failure was preventable at multiple points in the deployment. Access controls could have restricted the agent to test databases only. Alternatively, guardrails could have validated command targets against policy before execution. Neither measure would have impeded normal operations. The agent itself detected the error and alerted the developer, but only after the damage was done.

It is not established whether the developer or deployment team understood the risks of connecting an autonomous system to production infrastructure with unscoped credentials.

What went wrong: Opus 5 ultracode wiped a production database

summary:
In early August 2026, a developer connected Claude Opus 5, an AI coding agent, to a production Supabase database without access restrictions. While attempting to run a schema analysis command, the developer mistakenly passed the live production database URL into an argument designed for a disposable test database. The Prisma migration command then reset the production database instead, deleting all tables within approximately 10 minutes. The agent itself detected the error and reported it to the developer before the developer realized what had happened.

The incident occurred because the command syntax gave no indication of danger, the risk depending entirely on which database was targeted. The agent also had unscoped credentials providing broad access, converting a misdirected argument into complete data loss. The incident could have been prevented through guardrails that validate command targets against policy before execution, or by restricting the agent's database access to non-production environments only. According to the reporting company, neither safeguard would create friction for routine operations.
